extracted.intended_audience: Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina employees and staff responsible for internal and external written communications (marketing, program staff, managers)
extracted.subtask_description: A nonprofit organization's internal written-communications style guide for producing consistent, accessible, and on-brand internal and external materials (press releases, emails, flyers, signage, etc.). Covers naming conventions, grammar/style rules, accessibility, branding, and approval workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Company Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Our official company name is Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina, Inc. In formal communications, such as press releases, letters printed on company letterhead, articles, and legal documents, our full, official name should be used in the first instance followed by the shortened name in parentheses. This allows the use of “Goodwill” in all following instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other acceptable forms: Goodwill Industries of Northwest NC; Goodwill Industries of Northwest North Carolina; Goodwill; Goodwill Industries; Goodwill Northwest NC. Do not use: GoodwillNWNC, Goodwill NWNC, Goodwill Industries NWNC except as a hashtag or social media handle (e.g., #GoodwillNWNC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goodwill Locations — Career Center naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Career Center' is the umbrella term that encompasses all sites offering workforce development services, including Workforce Development Centers, Career Connections Centers, and partner sites/other locations. Workforce Development Centers are named according to the county in which they are located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal names such as 'Buncombe County Workforce Development Center' (include address where needed). For Career Connections Centers, use county-based names and you may abbreviate as Career Centers or Career Connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Connections Centers — naming/abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: Goodwill operates smaller centers called Career Connections Centers which can be abbreviated as Career Centers or Career Connections. These are also named by the county in which they are located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the county-based formal name on first reference; examples provided for consistency (e.g., 'Burke County Career Connections Center').

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce Development — partner site naming and special programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Many programs are offered in partnership with other nonprofit and government agencies. In formal communications, the full program or service name should be stated in the first instance and must include mention of partner agencies. In following instances, the program name can be abbreviated, and partners do not have to be mentioned again unless needed for context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Access Center Adult High School, offered in partnership with Asheville-Buncombe Technical Community College' → later 'Access Center'. Verify partner names/spelling and obtain approval to use any partner brands or logos prior to use; obtain files from authorized representatives—never cut and paste logos or brandmarks from websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Prosperity Center naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prosperity Center, a United Way collaborative with Financial Pathways of the Piedmont (Winston-Salem) should be referred to as The Prosperity Center, always preceded by 'The'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the first instance include partner attribution as appropriate; subsequent references may be abbreviated as 'The Prosperity Center'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donated Goods Retail Locations — store naming
rubrics_metrics.description: External communications should refer to Goodwill stores as 'Goodwill Store', 'Goodwill Outlet Store', or 'Goodwill Retail Store'. When needed for context, the city name should be used; in cities with more than one store include the street.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Goodwill Retail Store, Mooresville (Williamson Road)'; 'Goodwill Store, Asheville (Tunnel Road)'. Do not use internal store numbers or solely community references in external communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donation Centers — Attended Donation Centers (ADCs) naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Goodwill refers to its staffed donation centers as Attended Donation Centers, abbreviated as ADCs. For external communications the naming convention is City - Street (e.g., 'Kernersville – Main St').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that these centers are staffed (differentiator). For a full list, refer to the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce Development Terminology — program participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons enrolled in Goodwill’s workforce development programs or benefitting from Goodwill’s workforce development services are termed 'program participants'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Professional Center by Goodwill program participants can also be referred to as 'clients'. Distinguish branded program names (e.g., 'Project Re-entry') from generic terms ('reentry').

rubrics_metrics.name: Email Signature standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Outlook signature approved for all Goodwill employees should include: First M. Last; Job Title; Company Name; Office phone with extension; Email Address; Company Website URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided. Optional: include mobile and physical/mailing address. Do not 'customize' the signature template in any way (no colors, quotes, icons, images, logos, etc.). Consistency across organization is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible language — plain language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications must be clear and accessible; Goodwill staff should be committed to not talking down to anyone or using language, terminology or 'jargon' that could marginalize, offend, or confuse participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid complex sentence construction and long sentences; prefer two or three brief sentences. Use common language at ~9th-grade reading level. Use bulleted lists where possible. Avoid filler language (e.g., 'in order to…', '18 years of age'). Consider audience literacy and language barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inclusive language — person-focused and neutral terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Respectful language focuses on the person, not on physical appearance or other characteristics. Avoid making references to a person’s age, gender, ethnicity or race, religion, abilities or sexual orientation unless relevant to the program or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gender-neutral terms (use 'they' as acceptable singular). For disability, use person-first language (e.g., 'person with a disability' not 'disabled person'). For HIPAA/privacy: focus on person first and ensure participants consent to sharing personal information internally or externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: General writing and grammar guideline — word choice and jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Always use the simplest possible word and professional, easy-to-understand sentence construction. Avoid clichés.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the audience will understand jargon, acronyms, or special terms; when in doubt, spell them out. Use resources (Purdue OWL, Grammarly) for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and acronyms — first use spelled out
rubrics_metrics.description: The first time you use the term, write out its complete name. You can use the acronym or abbreviation thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Goodwill’s Donated Goods Retail (DGR). When writing acronyms, use capital letters with no periods (e.g., WFD, NC, NCDVR). Consider audience context before using acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses — USPS formatting and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing an envelope to mail via USPS, always use standard USPS abbreviations for street address and state, whether used in text or block address form. Use same guidelines when listing addresses on marketing materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example block format provided. NOTE: No comma between state abbreviation and ZIP Code. Verify street name spellings and include directional info (NE, SW). Use postal codes only in addresses; for place names see States and Cities section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ages — numerals and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to a person, use numerals for all ages. If using a person’s or object’s age as a description, use hyphens (e.g., 'A 39-year-old person').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General numbers rule applies elsewhere: spell out one to nine; use numerals for 10 and up (exceptions explained in Numbers section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates — format and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this format: Day, Month, Year (e.g., Friday, March 20, 2021). Do not use 'st, rd, or th' with dates in this format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not abbreviate days of week (except if space-limited in marketing). Months with five or fewer letters are not abbreviated; other months may be abbreviated (Jan., Feb., Aug., Sept., Oct., Nov., Dec.). When referencing only month and year, don't abbreviate month and do not use a comma (e.g., 'October 2021').

rubrics_metrics.name: Job titles — capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize formal titles only when they appear before a person’s name. Do not capitalize the title if it appears after the person’s name or if it is informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided. Generally do not capitalize occupations or occupational categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurements and distances — number formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the general numbers rule: Spell out numbers one through nine; use digits for 10 and up. Do not abbreviate units of measurement in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 47 miles; 2 feet; 10 inches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money — dollar symbol and cents conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the dollar symbol ($) for specific amounts. For even dollar amounts, do not include cents (e.g., $27 not $27.00). For amounts less than one dollar, write out the amount in words (e.g., two cents, not $0.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exception to the general numbers rule and applies only when using the dollar/symbol format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers — general rules and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out numbers one through nine and use digits for 10 and up. Do not begin a sentence with a number; spell it out instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use digits for addresses, ages of people, dates, money (when using symbols), and times. See other sections for more detailed exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentages — spelling out 'percent'
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out the word 'percent' when including percentages in a sentence instead of using the symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '10 percent' (not '10%').

rubrics_metrics.name: Phone numbers — formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Always use the full area code and phone number. Include an extension whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use parentheses or periods to separate sections. Example: 336-724-3621 ext. 11900.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and accepted style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: The major punctuation marks are period, comma, exclamation point, question mark, semi-colon, and colon. The guide does not provide exhaustive punctuation rules but points to external resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, consult Purdue OWL (link provided). The four primary style guides are AP, Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS), MLA, and APA. Oxford/serial comma: accepted, but review select statements on a case-by-case basis; examples shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: States and Cities (place names) — formatting and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out a state’s full name when using it by itself in a sentence. Use 'City name, State (abbreviated)' when referring to towns/cities (e.g., Marion, NC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For local audiences the state may be omitted. Use postal code abbreviations ONLY when writing addresses. Do not capitalize 'state', 'county', or 'city' unless part of a formal name (e.g., 'Forsyth County' vs 'the county').

rubrics_metrics.name: Times — formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred time format: 6 a.m. (not 6AM, 6 A.M., or 6am). If a time is on the hour, do not use ':00' (e.g., 8 a.m., not 8:00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: '6am' format for social media/digital/print advertising when space is limited. Use 'noon' and 'midnight' to avoid 12 p.m./12 a.m. confusion. Maintain consistency throughout the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes — frequently misused words and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists frequent errors (i.e., vs e.g., your vs you're, it's vs its, misplaced modifiers, irregardless vs regardless, affect vs effect, ensure vs insure) and explains correct usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tips include substituting words to test correctness (e.g., 'you are' for 'you're'), reading sentences aloud, and examples illustrating correct vs incorrect usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading is the process of reviewing the final draft for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and formatting consistency and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a break between composing and proofreading; read aloud; check for one type of error at a time; proof a hard copy if possible; have second or third set of eyes; build time for colleagues/Marketing Team to proof; when in doubt consult this guide or listed resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of logo and brandmarks — Marketing approval required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any creative materials seen or used by external audiences (flyers, brochures, presentations, videos, social posts, email campaigns, ads, posters, signs, branded apparel, promotional items, etc.) must be created by and/or approved by the Marketing Department (see Policy MD-800-005 on SharePoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are strict guidelines and compliance with Goodwill Industries International bylaws is required. Refer to Marketing SharePoint resources: brand guidelines for the Goodwill Industries of Northwest NC logo and the Smiling G logo; logo files. Contact marketing@goodwillnwnc.org for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images and copyrights — do not use unlicensed imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: All pictures, illustrations, icons, and imagery are automatically copyrighted and belong to the creator; unless specifically stated, you do not have the right to use images found online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using unlicensed images is unlawful and copyright infringement. The Marketing Department has licensed many assets—contact Marketing for needs. External-facing materials require Marketing review and approval prior to sharing.
